newsitem.title: GREECE: Optimism for OTE part-float spurs Greek stocks.
newsitem.headline: Optimism for OTE part-float spurs Greek stocks.

text.p: Early Wednesday trade on the Athens bourse was spiced by a late Tuesday announcement of the price range for state telecoms OTE part-floated shares and early indications of increased interest in the issue.
"The market has been dealt with positive news as regards the price range," said Costas Karydis, broker at DF Securities.
However, the range was wider than expected and we do not have official information as regards the volume of bids placed by institutional investors near the opposite ends of the band, he added.
OTE's shares will be offered to institutional investors at 6,200-6,900 drachmas per shares in the book-building which ends June 13.
It was joined on Wednesday by a public offering at 6,000-6,700 drachmas per share which also ends June 13.

The Greek State, currently owner of 92.43 percent of OTE's stock, offers a total of 45 million shares --10.7 percent -- but may increase the size of the offering by 2.1 million shares and global co-ordinators may allocate an extra 6.33 million shares at their discretion.
Brokers were pleased to see increased interest from international and domestic investors and said that the number of new investors was equally critical to the subscription rate to the issue.
"There is considerable demand for OTE's shares and the participation of foreign portfolios will affect the course of the broader market," said Karydis.
If the issue attracts more new investors than last year's IPO (160,000 retail investors), then the outcome on the oversubscription rate will be less important, he added.
Recent trading behaviour in OTE's shares was seen reflecting expectations of faster earnings growth.
"Trading of OTE's shares in the past few sessions reflects expectations of increased earnings growth potential, with the deal in Serbia contributing to this," said Karydis.
Investors snap up OTE shares which still trade cum of the rights issue, he added.
OTE signed a deal on Monday to acquire 20 percent of New Serbia's PTT and an equal percentage in a GSM operator in that country for 675 million marks.

Following the running part-flotation, OTE will tap the market with a 7.5 percent rights issue of 31.6 million shares at a 16 percent discount to its June 13 closing price, rounded to the nearest 100 drachmas.
The Athens general index was up 0.89 percent or 14.35 points at 1,618.19 from Tuesday's 1,603.84 close after 25 minutes of trading, with banks leading the market with a 1.04 percent climb.
Turnover amounted to 3.6 billion drachmas on volume of 0.63 million shares.
Advancers led decliners 94 to 35 with 19 shares unchanged on 148 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 1,118-1,148. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were 105 drachmas former at 7,210.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 636.16-676.76 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $80.20-$81.43. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 3,953-4,181 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $16.05-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted higher at 254-287 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
--Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
